propositions.text: Six judicial review applications challenge refusals of study and work permits and reconsideration requests due to misrepresentation.
propositions.quote: This decision addresses six applications for judicial review, brought by three members of the same family, challenging the refusal of their intertwined applications for study and work permits, as well as the refusal of their reconsideration requests.

propositions.text: Officer found Applicants inadmissible for misrepresentation using fraudulent academic transcripts.
propositions.quote: In those impugned decisions by an Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada [IRCC] officer [the Officer], the Officer found the Applicants inadmissible to Canada for misrepresentation due to the use of fraudulent academic transcripts in support of the study permit application of one of the Applicants.

paragraphs.summary: The court states six judicial review applications challenge refusals due to misrepresentation found by the Officer using fraudulent transcripts.

propositions.text: Applications are dismissed because the Officer’s procedure meets procedural fairness requirements.
propositions.quote: these applications are dismissed, because the Officer’s procedure as a whole satisfies the requirements of procedural fairness.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the applications, finding the Officer’s procedure satisfies procedural fairness.

propositions.text: Applicants are a family from the Philippines: Parents Lea Marie and Angelito, and son Paul Angelo (Principal Applicant).
propositions.quote: The Applicants are all citizens of the Philippines and members of the same family – Lea Marie Sampang and her spouse, Angelito Sampang [together, the Parents], and their son, Paul Angelo Sampang [the Principal Applicant].

propositions.text: In February 2023, Applicants submitted study and work permit applications.
propositions.quote: In February 2023, the Applicants submitted applications for study and work permits (along with study permit applications for other dependents of the Parents that are not material to the present matters).

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Applicants are a Filipino family who submitted study and work permit applications in February 2023.

propositions.text: In April 2023, IRCC requested a letter of acceptance from a Designated Learning Institution for the Principal Applicant.
propositions.quote: In April 2023, IRCC requested that the Principal Applicant submit a post-secondary education letter of acceptance [LOA] from a Designated Learning Institution [DLI].

propositions.text: On May 16, 2023, Applicants submitted an LOA from Centennial College, a Canadian DLI.
propositions.quote: On May 16, 2023, the Applicants submitted an LOA from Centennial College, which is a DLI in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The court states IRCC requested and Applicants submitted an LOA from Centennial College in 2023.

propositions.text: Principal Applicant reported document fraud/misrepresentation by family and himself to IRCC, attaching detailed evidence.
propositions.quote: I am writing this in order to report a case of document fraud/misrepresentation that was committed by my family and myself. Attached to this form is a pdf document detailing the situation in greater clarity...

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker records the Principal Applicant reported document fraud by his family and himself to IRCC with detailed evidence.

propositions.text: On June 12, 2023, Principal Applicant reiterated that he and family submitted forged transcripts, instructed by parents.
propositions.quote: the Principal Applicant reiterated the allegation that he and his family had furnished forged transcripts to Centennial College in order to obtain an LOA. The Principal Applicant stated that his parents had instructed him to doctor the transcripts

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker records the Principal Applicant admitted submitting forged transcripts under parental instruction.

propositions.text: On June 16, 2023, IRCC sent procedural fairness letters to Applicants outlining concerns about misrepresentation and inadmissibility.
propositions.quote: On June 16, 2023, IRCC sent each of the Applicants procedural fairness letters in materially the same form [the PFL], which included the following extract identifying IRCC’s concerns

propositions.text: PFL stated concerns about misrepresentation of travel purpose and academic history, joint enterprise to furnish non-bona fide transcripts.
propositions.quote: Specifically, I am concerned that you have misrepresented your purpose of travel to Canada and your academic history. I note here that you have engaged in a joint enterprise to furnish non-bona fide transcripts

propositions.text: PFL warned of inadmissibility for five years under section 40(1)(a) IRPA if misrepresentation found.
propositions.quote: Please note that if it is found that you have engaged in misrepresentation in submitting your application, you may be found to be inadmissible under section 40(1)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.

propositions.text: PFL offered opportunity to respond with explanation and documentation.
propositions.quote: I am offering you an opportunity to respond to our concerns by providing a detailed explanation as well as relevant documentation to support your response.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker sent PFLs detailing concerns about misrepresentation, inadmissibility, and offered Applicants chance to respond.

propositions.text: Parents responded to PFL denying wrongdoing and resubmitted school documents as genuine.
propositions.quote: The Parents responded to the PFL, stating that the Principal Applicant’s school documents submitted with his application were genuine and resubmitting those documents.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker records Parents denied wrongdoing and resubmitted school documents as genuine in response to PFL.

propositions.text: On September 2, 2023, Officer refused applications due to misrepresentation, finding Applicants inadmissible for five years.
propositions.quote: On September 2, 2023, the Officer refused the Applicants’ applications due to misrepresentation, and they were found to be inadmissible to Canada for a period of five years.

propositions.text: GCMS notes show Officer reviewed submissions, found son’s admission credible and parents’ denials less credible.
propositions.quote: I place greater weight on the first submission and admission of capability [sic], it is spontaneous and provides substantiating documents which correspond to our own information on file.

propositions.text: Officer satisfied that son misrepresented by submitting non-bona fide transcripts to obtain LOA and study permit.
propositions.quote: I am satisfied that the PA has misrepresented, above are the reasons.

propositions.text: Officer noted misrepresentation would not have been detected without careful examination of submitted information.
propositions.quote: I note that had it not been detected by the careful examination of the information submitted by the PA to our office, this possible misrepresentation would not have been noted or open to the decision maker to review.

propositions.text: Officer considered truthful declaration of purpose and submission of non bona fide documents material to decision.
propositions.quote: Lastly, I consider the full and truthful declaration of a PA’s purpose of travel and activities coordinating to deceive by providing non bona fide education documents to be material facts when examining an app

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker refused applications for misrepresentation, finding son’s admission credible and misrepresentation material.

propositions.text: Parents learned of son’s self-sabotage only after receiving GCMS notes around September 30, 2023.
propositions.quote: On or around September 30, 2023, the Parents received a copy of the GCMS notes related to the Refusal Decisions. The Applicants assert that it was only at that stage that the Parents discovered that the Principal Applicant had self-sabotaged his application

propositions.text: On October 31, 2023, Applicants submitted reconsideration requests with benefit of new information.
propositions.quote: With the benefit of this information, on October 31, 2023, the Applicants submitted requests for reconsideration of the Refusal Decisions.

propositions.text: On November 9, 2023, Officer refused reconsideration requests, finding no new evidence and rejecting Parents’ claim son acted alone.
propositions.quote: On November 9, 2023, in the decisions under review in the other three of the within applications for judicial review... the Officer refused the reconsideration requests [the Reconsideration Decisions]. The Officer’s GCMS notes provide reasons... I reject this contention on their part that the son was acting completely of his own volition

paragraphs.summary: Applicants learned of son’s sabotage after GCMS notes, requested reconsideration, which Officer refused, rejecting son acted alone.

propositions.text: Associate Judge Trent Horne consolidated all six judicial review applications on December 21, 2023.
propositions.quote: On December 21, 2023, at the request of the Applicants and upon the consent of the Respondent, Associate Judge Trent Horne issued an Order consolidating all six applications for judicial review.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the six judicial review applications were consolidated by order on December 21, 2023.

propositions.text: Applicants identify issues: whether Refusal Decisions were unreasonable due to insufficiently specific PFL, and whether Reconsideration Decisions were unreasonable due to procedural fairness breaches.
propositions.quote: The Applicants’ written submissions describe the following issues for the Court’s determination: Are the Refusal Decisions unreasonable, because the PFL was not sufficiently specific as to the Officer’s concerns... Are the Reconsideration Decisions unreasonable, because the Officer relied therein on credibility findings without affording the Applicants requisite procedural fairness?

paragraphs.summary: Applicants submit issues: Refusal Decisions unreasonable for insufficient PFL specificity; Reconsideration Decisions unreasonable for procedural fairness breaches.

propositions.text: Procedural fairness issues require correctness standard, not reasonableness, per Canadian Pacific Railway v Canada (Attorney General).
propositions.quote: both issues raise considerations of procedural fairness, which are governed by a standard akin to correctness, requiring the Court to assess whether... the process... was fair (Canadian Pacific Railway Company v Canada (Attorney General), 2018 FCA 69 at para 54).

propositions.text: Applicants initially submitted reasonableness standard applies but later adopted correctness standard for procedural fairness issues.
propositions.quote: their written submissions asserted that the reasonableness standard applies... At the hearing... the Applicants’ counsel revisited their submission on standard of review, adopting the position that the standard of correctness governs.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains procedural fairness issues require correctness standard; Applicants initially argued reasonableness but later adopted correctness.

propositions.text: Applicants advance only procedural fairness arguments, not merits, and only on behalf of Parents, not Principal Applicant.
propositions.quote: Applicants’ counsel confirmed... advancing solely procedural fairness arguments, not arguments related to the merits... only on behalf of the Parents, not on behalf of the Principal Applicant.

propositions.text: Principal Applicant no longer seeks to impugn Officer’s decisions relating to him.
propositions.quote: the Principal Applicant is no longer seeking to impugn the Officer’s decisions as they relate to him.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue only procedural fairness issues on behalf of Parents; Principal Applicant no longer challenges decisions relating to him.

propositions.text: Court will reformulate Applicants’ issues to reflect procedural fairness arguments accurately.
propositions.quote: In analysing the procedural fairness arguments raised by the Applicants, I will reformulate below the articulation of the Applicants’ issues, to accurately reflect above.

paragraphs.summary: The court will reformulate the Applicants’ issues to accurately reflect procedural fairness arguments.

propositions.text: Applicants acknowledge receiving PFL but argue it was insufficiently specific to alert Parents to source of Officer’s concerns.
propositions.quote: The Applicants acknowledge that they received a PFL from IRCC and were therefore aware of the Officer’s concerns... However, they argue that the contents of the PFL were insufficient to alert the Parents to the source of the Officer’s concerns

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue PFL was insufficiently specific to alert Parents to source of Officer’s concerns despite receiving it.

propositions.text: Parents unaware of Confession Letters and not complicit in transcript alteration; lack of specific PFL deprived them of procedural fairness.
propositions.quote: The Applicants submit that the Parents were not aware of the Confession Letters, had not been aware of or complicit in the Principal Applicant’s alteration of his transcripts... and were therefore deprived of procedural fairness

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue Parents’ lack of awareness and insufficient PFL deprived them of procedural fairness.

propositions.text: Respondent argues PFL contents were sufficient to notify Parents of Officer’s concerns; no requirement to specify source explicitly.
propositions.quote: The Respondent disagrees, arguing that the contents of the PFL were sufficient to place the Parents on notice... The Respondent submits that the Officer’s procedural fairness obligations did not include a requirement to identify more explicitly the precise source of the concern.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues PFL was sufficiently specific and no explicit source identification was required for procedural fairness.

propositions.text: Court raised whether procedural fairness breach was remedied by Applicants learning source of concerns after Refusal Decisions and submitting reconsideration requests.
propositions.quote: the Court raised with counsel the question whether the asserted breach of procedural fairness was in any event remedied by the fact that... the Applicants learned of the source of the Officer’s concerns and... submitted a request for reconsideration

propositions.text: Court requested submissions on Weldesenbet v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2022 FC 1174, which considered similar procedural fairness issues in reconsideration.
propositions.quote: The Court drew counsel’s attention to the decision in Weldesenbet v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2022 FC 1174... The Court requested submissions on that authority and the principles canvassed therein

paragraphs.summary: The court raised whether procedural fairness breach was remedied by reconsideration and requested submissions on Weldesenbet case.

propositions.text: Weldesenbet involved permanent residence application dismissed, reconsidered, and judicial review of both decisions due to procedural fairness concerns.
propositions.quote: Weldesenbet involved an application for permanent residence on humanitarian and compassionate grounds, which an IRCC officer dismissed... The applicant then sought judicial review of both the original decision and the reconsideration decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court describes Weldesenbet case involving reconsideration and judicial review over procedural fairness in permanent residence application.

propositions.text: Applicant in Weldesenbet argued deprivation of procedural fairness due to incompetent representation regarding original decision
propositions.quote: the applicant in Weldesenbet again argued that she had been deprived of procedural fairness due to incompetent representation regarding the original decision

propositions.text: Court found reconsideration remedied alleged breach of procedural fairness
propositions.quote: the Court found that the reconsideration had remedied the alleged breach of procedural fairness

propositions.text: Alleged breach by former representative had no material effect because applicant could file new evidence on reconsideration
propositions.quote: The alleged breach by the former representative did not have a material effect, because the applicant was permitted to file new evidence on reconsideration

propositions.text: Procedure as a whole satisfied procedural fairness requirements; no live controversy remained on alleged breach
propositions.quote: The Court found that the procedure as a whole satisfied the requirements of procedural fairness and that there was therefore no longer a live controversy between the parties in relation to the alleged breach

paragraphs.summary: Applicant in Weldesenbet argued procedural fairness breach; earlier court found reconsideration remedied breach and procedure was fair, ending controversy.

propositions.text: Applicants argue Weldesenbet is distinguishable because that applicant understood case and could submit evidence on reconsideration
propositions.quote: The Applicants argues that Weldesenbet is distinguishable because, unlike in the matter at hand, the applicant in Weldesenbet had a full understanding of the case it had to meet and, in connection with the reconsideration, an opportunity to submit additional evidence to meet that case

propositions.text: Applicants emphasize PFL did not identify existence of Confession Letters unlike Weldesenbet
propositions.quote: The Applicants contrast those circumstances with the matter at hand, emphasizing their position that the PFL did not identify the existence of the Confession Letters

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue Weldesenbet differs because that applicant understood case and PFL here failed to identify Confession Letters.

propositions.text: Respondent says Weldesenbet applies and any PFL defect was cured by opportunity to file new evidence after GCMS notes disclosure
propositions.quote: The Respondent takes the position that Weldesenbet is on point and, regardless of whether the PFL was inadequate and deprived the Applicants of requisite procedural fairness in connection with the Refusal Decisions, that defect was cured by affording the Applicants the opportunity to file new evidence and submissions, after the Applicants received the GCMS notes that identified the particular concerns that led to the Refusal Decisions, and the Officer’s subsequent consideration of that evidence and submissions in making the Reconsideration Decisions

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues Weldesenbet applies and any PFL defect was cured by allowing new evidence after GCMS notes disclosure.

propositions.text: Facts in Weldesenbet differ somewhat, as that case involved inadequate representation, not failure to alert applicant to case
propositions.quote: I accept the Applicants’ argument that the facts underlying Weldesenbet are somewhat distinct from those in the matter at hand. In particular, the procedural fairness issue in Weldesenbet concerned inadequate representation, not a concern that the applicant had not been alerted to the case she needed to meet

propositions.text: No principled basis to distinguish Weldesenbet reasoning
propositions.quote: I find no principled basis to distinguish the reasoning in Weldesenbet

paragraphs.summary: Court accepts Weldesenbet facts differ but finds no principled basis to distinguish its reasoning.

propositions.text: Applicants assert PFL was deficient for failing to alert Parents to Officer’s concerns from Confession Letters
propositions.quote: The Applicants assert that the PFL was deficient, in that it failed to alert the Parents to the Officer’s specific concerns arising from the Confession Letters

propositions.text: Mother’s statutory declaration states receipt of Refusal Decisions, GCMS notes, discovery of self-sabotage, confession, and Parents’ prior unawareness
propositions.quote: in the Statutory Declaration sworn by Principal Applicant’s mother on October 31, 2023... she states that: (a) on September 2, 2023, she and her family received the Refusal Decisions; (b) on or around September 30, 2023, she received a copy of the related GCMS notes, at which point she discovered that the Principal Applicant had self-sabotaged his study permit application by using an altered transcript and later informing IRCC what he had done; (c) the Principal Applicant confessed to his actions when the Parents questioned him about the Officer’s reasoning in the GCMS notes; and (d) the Parents were not aware of the Principal Applicant’s actions until they received a copy of the GCMS notes

paragraphs.summary: Applicants say PFL was deficient; mother’s declaration recounts receipt of decisions, GCMS notes, confession, and prior unawareness.

propositions.text: Parents submitted evidence in reconsideration; Officer considered it in Reconsideration Decisions
propositions.quote: the Parents submitted this evidence in support of their reconsideration request, and it is clear from the Reconsideration Decisions that the Officer took that evidence into account

propositions.text: Officer did not accept explanations but Parents were aware of case and had opportunity to respond by Reconsideration Decisions
propositions.quote: While the Officer did not accept those explanations as a basis to alter the Refusal Decisions, it is clear that by the time the Reconsideration Decisions were made, the Parents were aware of the case they had to meet and had been provided an opportunity to do so

propositions.text: Weldesenbet reasoning applies; any prior procedural fairness breach was remedied; no basis for Court intervention
propositions.quote: I therefore find that the reasoning in Weldesenbet applies and that any previous breach of procedural fairness arising from the alleged deficiencies in the PFL had been remedied. The procedure as a whole satisfies the requirements of procedural fairness, and there is no basis for the Court to intervene

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Parents submitted evidence considered by Officer; Weldesenbet applies; prior breach remedied; no intervention needed.

propositions.text: Applicants raise procedural fairness concerns about Reconsideration Decisions
propositions.quote: The Applicants also raise procedural fairness concerns about the Reconsideration Decisions

paragraphs.summary: Applicants raise procedural fairness concerns about Reconsideration Decisions.

propositions.text: Applicants argue Officer made adverse credibility finding without affording opportunity to respond, breaching procedural fairness
propositions.quote: The Applicants argue that this analysis demonstrates the Officer making an adverse credibility finding and that, in such circumstances, procedural fairness requires credibility concerns to be put to an applicant for an opportunity to respond before such findings are made

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue Officer made adverse credibility finding without chance to respond, breaching procedural fairness.

propositions.text: Respondent disputes characterization, says Officer’s reasoning was based on sufficiency of evidence, so no procedural fairness obligation arises
propositions.quote: The Respondent disputes this characterization of the Reconsideration Decisions, arguing that the Officer’s reasoning was based on the sufficiency of the Applicants’ evidence, such that no procedural fairness obligation arises

paragraphs.summary: Respondent disputes adverse credibility finding, says Officer based decision on evidence sufficiency, no fairness breach.

propositions.text: Court raised question whether procedural fairness principles apply given Applicants knew they had to respond to misrepresentation concerns
propositions.quote: the Court raised with counsel at the hearing the question whether the procedural fairness principles upon which the Applicants relied were applicable, given the broader context in which the Applicants were aware that they were required to respond to the Officer’s concerns

propositions.text: Court referred to Alalami decision on procedural fairness and credibility findings and requested submissions
propositions.quote: I drew counsel’s attention to this Court’s decision in Alalami v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2018 FC 328 [Alalami], which had considered an allegedly procedurally unfair process in which a visa officer made a misrepresentation finding based on credibility concerns

paragraphs.summary: Court questioned applicability of procedural fairness principles and referred to Alalami decision, requesting submissions.

propositions.text: In Alalami, applicant got procedural fairness letter about misrepresentation concerns and responded with explanation
propositions.quote: In Alalami, the applicant sought a temporary resident visa to visit Canada, and the officer sent him a procedural fairness letter, expressing concern that he had misrepresented his travel and immigration history. The applicant responded that he had made a mistake, having misread the relevant application form

propositions.text: Officer found applicant inadmissible for misrepresentation after explanation
propositions.quote: following which the officer found him inadmissible for misrepresentation

propositions.text: Applicant argued deprivation of procedural fairness because officer made negative credibility finding without opportunity to respond
propositions.quote: The applicant argued that he was deprived of procedural fairness because the officer based the decision on a negative credibility determination without affording him an opportunity to respond to the credibility concerns

paragraphs.summary: Alalami involved procedural fairness letter, applicant’s explanation, and claim of unfairness due to credibility finding without response chance.

propositions.text: Procedural fairness requires notice and opportunity to respond before misrepresentation findings
propositions.quote: I accept that the principles of procedural fairness must be applied before findings of misrepresentation are made

propositions.text: PFL explained issue and gave opportunity to respond; no requirement to advise officer disbelieved explanation or give further chance
propositions.quote: I do not consider the principles of procedural fairness to require the Officer to have advised Mr. Alalami that he did not accept the explanation and to have afforded him a further opportunity to comment before arriving at the Decision

propositions.text: PFL was sufficient to put applicant on notice including possibility explanation would not be accepted
propositions.quote: The PFL was sufficient to put Mr. Alalami on notice of the issue, including the possibility that the resulting explanation would not be accepted

propositions.text: No error found in procedure under correctness standard
propositions.quote: Applying the standard of correctness, I find no error in the procedure followed in arriving at the Decision

paragraphs.summary: Alalami held PFL was sufficient notice; no need to advise disbelief or give further chance; no procedural error found.

propositions.text: Applicants argue Alalami is distinguishable because no concerns about adequacy of PFL there, unlike here
propositions.quote: The Applicants argue that Alalami is distinguishable, because there were no concerns in that case about the adequacy of the procedural fairness letter employed by the officer

propositions.text: Applicants emphasize PFL here was insufficient and led to Officer’s credibility concern and negative decisions
propositions.quote: the Applicants emphasize their position that the PFL employed by the Officer in the matter at hand was insufficient and ultimately led to the Officer’s credibility concern and resulting negative Reconsideration Decisions

paragraphs.summary: Applicants say Alalami differs because PFL adequacy was not disputed there but is here, causing credibility concerns.

propositions.text: Respondent argues Alalami is determinative and precludes finding procedural fairness deprivation here
propositions.quote: The Respondent argues that Alalami is determinative of the procedural fairness issue the Applicants raise in connection with the Reconsideration Decisions

propositions.text: Even if finding is credibility, Alalami reasoning precludes procedural fairness breach conclusion
propositions.quote: even if the relevant finding were to be characterized as one of credibility rather than sufficiency of evidence, the Alalami reasoning precludes a conclusion that the Applicants were deprived of procedural fairness

paragraphs.summary: Respondent says Alalami controls and precludes procedural fairness breach even if finding is credibility.

propositions.text: Alalami is not fully on point because PFL adequacy was undisputed there but is challenged here
propositions.quote: I take the Applicants’ point that Alalami is not on all fours with the matter at hand. In Alalami, the Court’s conclusion that the process was procedurally fair turned on the notice that was given to the applicant through the procedural fairness letter, the adequacy of which was not in dispute

propositions.text: Here, due to Weldesenbet reasoning, Court did not need to decide PFL adequacy but Applicants challenge it
propositions.quote: while (because of the application of the reasoning in Weldesenbet), it has not been necessary for the Court to adjudicate the Applicants’ argument surrounding the adequacy of the PFL, the Applicants do challenge that adequacy

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Alalami differs as PFL adequacy undisputed there but challenged here; Weldesenbet reasoning avoided deciding it.

propositions.text: Regardless of PFL adequacy, Applicants knew case by Reconsideration Decisions and responded
propositions.quote: Regardless of the adequacy of the PFL, by the time of the Reconsideration Decisions, the Applicants (including the Parents) knew the case they had to meet

propositions.text: Assuming adverse credibility finding, procedural fairness did not require further opportunity to respond before Reconsideration Decisions
propositions.quote: Even assuming the Officer’s resulting analysis to have involved an adverse credibility finding, I do not consider the principles of procedural fairness to have required the Officer to advise the Applicants that he did not accept their explanation and afford them a further opportunity to comment before arriving at the Reconsideration Decisions

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes Applicants knew case and even if adverse credibility finding, no further response opportunity was required.

propositions.text: No basis for Court intervention found
propositions.quote: Again, I find no basis for the Court to intervene in this matter

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no basis for intervention.

propositions.text: Applications for judicial review dismissed; no question certified for appeal
propositions.quote: these applications for judicial review must be dismissed. Neither party proposed any question for certification for appeal, and none is stated

paragraphs.summary: Court dismisses judicial review applications and certifies no question for appeal.
